mechanism_narrative: When the FEDFUNDS rate rises by more than 0.25% over the next month, higher discount rates reduce the present value of expected corporate cash flows, leading to negative S&P 500 20-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS increases by >0.25% in the following month
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not statistically different from zero during the identified FEDFUNDS increase (p > 0.05) or FEDFUNDS rise is <0.25%.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly increase in PAYEMS (employment) by at least 50,000 jobs coincides with stronger consumer demand, which elevates equity risk premia and produces positive S&P 500 60-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases by ≥50,000 in the following month
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are negative or insignificant during the identified employment surge (t-test p ≥ 0.10).

mechanism_narrative: When HOUST (retail sales) exceeds 600K units for two consecutive months, it signals resilient consumer demand, which supports higher corporate earnings growth and positive S&P 500 20-day forward returns.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are negative during the identified high-demand window (median < 0).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in INDPRO (industrial production) of 2% or more indicates supply-side weakness, which raises uncertainty and produces negative S&P 500 20-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO decreases by ≥2% in the following month
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive or not significantly different from zero during the supply contraction (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When UNRATE (unemployment) falls below 7% for three consecutive months, it suggests labor market tightness that lowers risk aversion, resulting in positive S&P 500 5-day forward returns.
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are not statistically positive during the unemployment decline (p ≥ 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp monthly drop in PAYEMS (job creation) of 100,000 or more is accompanied by elevated uncertainty, which raises the cost of capital and drives negative S&P 500 20-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS decreases by ≥100,000 in the following month
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative during the job loss episode (p ≥ 0.10).

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous monthly increases in GDPC1 (GDP) and RSAFS (retail sales) above their prior month's levels by at least 2% each create a dual-demand signal that supports optimism and positive S&P 500 60-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 ↑ ≥2% AND RSAFS ↑ ≥2% in the following month
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive during the dual-demand episode (p ≥ 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: During a regime of persistent CPIAUCSL (CPI) inflation above 2.5%, the S&P 500 20-day forward return is expected to be negative due to higher discounting of expected cash flows.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive or not significantly different from zero when CPIAUCSL > 2.5% (p ≥ 0.05).
